milestones.title: Milestone and DAG driven development
milestones.problem: Work in this repository was planned in conversation and in task records that describe one session at a time. There was no executable specification of an outcome, no dependency graph between pieces of work, and no way for a fresh worker to ask the repository what to do next. The tool supervises a task; nothing supervised the plan the task belonged to.
milestones.outcome: Every non-trivial change in this repository belongs to a milestone specification and to one dependency-linked issue execution contract, validated as a DAG, with status derived rather than asserted, and projected to GitHub and to the website from that one canonical model.
milestones.current_state: The canonical model, its engine, its CLI, its projections, its doctrines and its tests exist and are exercised by this milestone's own issues. GitHub carried no issues and no milestones before this work.
milestones.desired_state: A fresh worker with no conversation history runs `majordomus plan next`, receives one issue, executes it inside its declared scope, attaches evidence, and the graph recomputes what is ready without anybody editing a status field.
non_scope: A hosted planning backend or database
A second project-management vocabulary; milestones and issues are the only new nouns
Bidirectional GitHub write-back into the canonical files
Estimation, burndown, velocity or any scheduling model
acceptance_criteria: The canonical model parses, rejects unknown keys, and refuses a duplicate id
A dependency cycle, a self-dependency and an unknown dependency are each rejected with a named finding
READY, BLOCKED, ACTIVE, VERIFY, DONE and CANCELLED are derived from recorded facts and stored nowhere
Execution waves are computed from the graph, and overlapping scope inside one wave is reported
The Mermaid DAG is generated from the same graph the CLI reads
GitHub milestones and issues are created and updated from the canonical model, and drift between them is reported
The website renders the roadmap, every milestone, every issue and the DAG from generated data
Every surface agrees: the CLI, the site data and the GitHub projection report the same issue set and the same READY set
Changing one dependency changes every surface
CI refuses a push whose canonical model is invalid or whose generated artifacts are stale
risks: The engine is shell and awk; a graph large enough to make that slow would need a different implementation. Measured, not assumed.
GitHub is a projection. If a human edits a generated issue body, the next sync reports drift rather than silently overwriting it, which means drift can accumulate unattended.

issues.title: Audit what actually plans work in this repository
non_scope: Any change to behaviour
issues.objective: Establish an evidence-backed map of how work is currently planned, tracked and remembered here, so that the model that replaces it is built against reality rather than against the README.
issues.why: Every later issue depends on knowing what already exists. The repository already has a canonical-to-derived architecture for claims, doctrines and the website; a planning model that ignored it would be a second architecture.
issues.current_state: Planning lived in task records, handovers, checkpoints and decisions. GitHub had no milestones and no issues. There was no dependency relation between pieces of work anywhere.
issues.desired_state: The current-state map exists, backed by commands anyone can rerun, and the schema work that follows cites it.
acceptance_criteria: The GitHub milestone and issue inventory is measured, not assumed
The existing canonical-to-derived pipeline is identified so the new model reuses it
The portability constraints that bound the implementation are named

evidence.command: gh issue list --state all --limit 50; gh api repos/korczis/prismatic-majordomus/milestones
evidence.result: both empty: the repository had no GitHub issues and no milestones before this milestone

issues.title: Define the canonical milestone and issue schema
non_scope: JSON Schema; this repository validates with allowlists and its own YAML subset
A separate evidence directory; evidence lives inside the record it proves
issues.objective: Define the smallest repository-native representation of a milestone outcome specification and an issue execution contract, and enforce it the way every other configuration file here is enforced: a key nobody reads is an error.
issues.why: Every surface downstream reads these files. A field that is written and never read, or read and never written, becomes a lie that the website eventually publishes.
issues.current_state: Policy, profiles and prompts each have an allowlist under share/allow. Milestones and issues had none because they did not exist.
issues.desired_state: share/allow/project.txt, share/allow/milestone.txt and share/allow/issue.txt exist and every key in a canonical file matches one of them.
acceptance_criteria: An unknown key in a milestone or issue file is a reported failure
No status field exists in either schema
Evidence is part of the record whose completion it gates
issues.risk: A schema too small forces a later migration; a schema too large invites fields nobody reads.

issues.title: Implement the model loader and the status derivation engine
non_scope: Any status field a human can set directly
issues.objective: Load every canonical file into one normalised model and derive issue and milestone status from recorded facts, in exactly one implementation that every surface calls.
issues.why: Four surfaces need to know what is READY. Four implementations of READY is four answers. One engine is the whole architecture.
issues.desired_state: lib/project.sh loads the files, lib/project.awk derives the model, and the CLI, the site generator and the GitHub adapter all read that model.
acceptance_criteria: Issue status is derived from started_at, verified_at, completed_at, cancelled, evidence coverage and dependency state
Milestone status is derived from its issues and its own evidence
The active milestone is derived from order and status, not declared
A completed issue whose required evidence is missing derives VERIFY, not DONE
issues.risk: bash 3.2 has no associative arrays; the graph work is done in awk, which does.

issues.title: Implement DAG validation and execution waves
non_scope: Estimation or critical-path scheduling
issues.objective: Validate the dependency graph and derive topological execution waves, refusing every malformed graph with a named finding rather than a guess.
issues.why: A dependency list without validation is a suggestion. A cycle that nobody detects becomes a set of issues that can never be ready and nobody can explain why.
issues.desired_state: Unknown, self and duplicate dependencies, duplicate ids and cycles are each rejected by name, and waves are computed by Kahn layering.
acceptance_criteria: A cycle is detected and the issues inside it are named
A self-dependency and an unknown dependency are each a distinct finding
Waves place an issue one layer past its deepest dependency
Two issues sharing a wave and a scope path are reported as serialised

issues.title: Implement the plan command surface
non_scope: Any network call; the CLI never leaves the machine
issues.objective: Give a worker one command that answers what is ready, why something is blocked, what the graph looks like, and that moves an issue through its lifecycle while refusing illegal transitions.
issues.why: A model nobody can query is a filing cabinet. The command is how a fresh session with no conversation history finds its work.
issues.current_state: The engine existed with no interface.
issues.desired_state: majordomus plan validate, status, list, show, ready, blocked, waves, graph, next, body, start, verify, evidence and done all read the one model.
acceptance_criteria: plan start refuses an issue that is not READY
plan done refuses while a required evidence token has no evidence
plan evidence refuses a token the issue does not require
plan evidence refuses without a command or an artifact
every subcommand answers --help and an unknown one exits 2

issues.title: Generate the Mermaid DAG from the graph
non_scope: Layout tuning beyond what Mermaid decides
issues.objective: Render the dependency graph as Mermaid from the same edges the engine derives, so that no diagram anywhere is drawn by hand.
issues.why: A hand-drawn dependency diagram is a second source of truth that is wrong the first time an edge changes.
issues.current_state: The site rendered Mermaid for architecture diagrams written by hand in Markdown.
issues.desired_state: majordomus plan graph emits the DAG, and the docs, the site and the GitHub milestone body all use that output.
acceptance_criteria: Every node in the diagram is an issue in the model and every edge is a dependency in the model
Node styling reflects derived status
Restricting to one milestone emits only that milestone's subgraph

issues.title: Enforce the canonical model as doctrine
non_scope: Blocking a commit on a work-in-progress issue; progress is reported, not blocked
issues.objective: Add the project model to the doctrine registry so that doctor reports a broken model and watch reports a model that has drifted, through the same dispatcher every other rule uses.
issues.why: A rule enforced by a script nobody runs is documentation. The doctrine registry is how this repository makes enforcement verifiable end to end.
issues.current_state: The registry covered policy, profiles, scope, state, notes, projections and retention. Nothing covered the plan.
issues.desired_state: project_integrity and dag_integrity are declared, have validator functions, are dispatched by doctor and watch, and each has a test.
acceptance_criteria: A repository with no canonical model skips both doctrines rather than failing
An invalid model is a blocking doctor failure with a reproduce command
watch reports the same violations as drift
issues.risk: A doctrine that fails in a repository without a project model would make every user installation red.

issues.title: Project the model to GitHub milestones and issues
non_scope: Writing GitHub state back into the canonical files
Any network call inside bin, lib, share or test
issues.objective: Create and update GitHub milestones and issues from the canonical model, report drift instead of overwriting human edits, and keep every network call out of the tool itself.
issues.why: GitHub is where collaboration happens, so it must show the plan. It is not where the plan lives, so it must never be the thing that defines it.
issues.current_state: The repository had no GitHub issues or milestones at all.
issues.desired_state: scripts/github-sync renders the projection from majordomus plan body, creates what is missing, updates what changed, and reports what a human has edited.
acceptance_criteria: The adapter runs offline against a fixture and produces the exact payload it would post
A managed issue whose body differs from the projection is reported as drift, not overwritten
A closed issue whose canonical status is not DONE is reported
The tool itself contains no network client
issues.risk: A sync that overwrites a human comment thread would make GitHub hostile to use.

issues.title: Project the model into the website
non_scope: Any hand-written roadmap content
issues.objective: Generate the roadmap, every milestone page, every issue page and the DAG page from the canonical model through the existing site data pipeline.
issues.why: The website already derives every capability claim from a canonical file. A hand-written roadmap page beside it would be the one page that can be wrong.
issues.current_state: The site derived project, profiles, policy, claims, doctrines, commands and docs. It had no roadmap.
issues.desired_state: site/data/generated/plan.json exists, and the roadmap, milestone, issue and DAG routes render from it and from nothing else.
acceptance_criteria: The generated data contains every milestone and issue with its derived status and wave
The roadmap, milestone, issue and DAG routes exist and are reachable from navigation
The pages are mobile-first and the DAG stays readable on a narrow screen
Stale generated data fails the sync check

evidence.result: site-check: 0 failure(s); every milestone and issue has a page, every canonical edge appears in the rendered graph, every READY issue is linked from /plan/

issues.risk: The site build is the slowest surface; a regression here is found late.

issues.title: Behavioural tests for schema, status, graph and command
non_scope: Property-based testing frameworks
issues.objective: Prove each rule of the model with a case that fails when the rule is removed, in a disposable repository, the way every other rule here is proven.
issues.why: The repository forbids a capability sentence without a test behind it. The model makes several capability sentences.
issues.desired_state: Cases cover the schema, status derivation, the graph, the waves, the command surface and the doctrine wiring.
acceptance_criteria: A duplicate id, an unknown dependency, a self-dependency and a cycle each have a negative case
READY, BLOCKED, ACTIVE, VERIFY and DONE each have a case
Wave assignment has a case with a diamond dependency
Every case runs in a disposable repository, never against this checkout

issues.title: Cross-surface consistency and mutation tests
non_scope: Live GitHub calls in the test suite
issues.objective: Prove that the CLI, the generated site data and the GitHub projection describe the same graph, and that changing one canonical dependency changes all of them.
issues.why: One engine is a claim. A test that compares the surfaces is the only thing that keeps it true after the next change.
issues.current_state: Each surface was tested on its own.
issues.desired_state: A case compares the issue set, the READY set and the edge set across surfaces, and a second case mutates a dependency and asserts every surface moved.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical issue count equals CLI count equals site data count equals projection count
Canonical READY set equals the CLI READY set equals the site data READY set
Canonical edges equal Mermaid edges equal site data edges
Adding one dependency changes status, waves, Mermaid and site data together

issues.title: Make CI refuse an invalid model or a stale projection
non_scope: Any CI step that needs a GitHub token to pass
issues.objective: Add the model validation and the projection freshness check to the blocking CI job, with no advisory pass.
issues.why: A validator that runs only when somebody remembers is not enforcement.
issues.current_state: CI ran the suite, doctor, watch and the site data sync check.
issues.desired_state: CI also runs plan validate and the offline GitHub projection check, and fails on either.
acceptance_criteria: plan validate runs in the blocking job and its exit code is not swallowed
The GitHub projection is checked offline against the canonical model
No new step requires network access to succeed

issues.title: Document the semantics and the dogfooding rule
non_scope: Any count, progress figure or status written in prose
issues.objective: Write the human documentation that explains why the model exists and what its terms mean, and leave every current fact to be generated.
issues.why: Documentation that states current state goes stale. Documentation that states semantics does not. The split has to be deliberate or the first roadmap paragraph rots.
issues.current_state: docs explained the task lifecycle and the doctrine chain, and nothing explained the plan.
issues.desired_state: docs/PLANNING.md explains the model and docs/DOGFOODING.md states the rule that Majordomus cannot recommend a discipline it does not use.
acceptance_criteria: The documents explain semantics and contain no current-state figures
Every command they name exists and answers --help
Both appear on the website through the existing docs pipeline

evidence.result: site data: in sync (bb6614bc9be5); docs/PLANNING.md and docs/DOGFOODING.md indexed and rendered

issues.title: Make the worker instructions require the model
non_scope: Provider-specific wording; the body is provider neutral
issues.objective: Change the always-loaded provider instructions so that a fresh worker of any provider selects work through the model rather than from conversation or a TODO list.
issues.why: The model only becomes the way work happens if the file every worker loads first says so.
issues.current_state: The projection body described the task lifecycle and said nothing about milestones, issues or dependencies.
issues.desired_state: The generated CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md carry the plan lifecycle, and the projections stay inside their line budget.
acceptance_criteria: The always-loaded projection instructs a worker to take work from plan next
The projection stays within the policy line budget
Regenerating the projections produces no diff

evidence.command: bin/majordomus update && bin/majordomus doctor && bin/majordomus watch
evidence.result: CLAUDE.md 132 lines within the 150 budget; links resolve; no hardcoded counts; doctor 0 failures; watch reports no projection drift

issues.risk: The always-loaded budget is a hard cap; adding text can push the projection over it.

issues.title: Open the first real milestone and execute one issue through it
non_scope: A synthetic demonstration milestone
issues.objective: Prove the system on real repository work: open a milestone that exists because the repository needs it, and take one of its issues from READY to DONE entirely through the model.
issues.why: Infrastructure that has never carried real work is a demo. The cutover is the only evidence that the discipline is usable.
issues.current_state: M000 was executed partly outside the system, because the system did not exist when it began.
issues.desired_state: A real post-bootstrap milestone exists, one of its issues is DONE with evidence recorded through plan evidence, and the graph has recomputed the next ready issue.
acceptance_criteria: The milestone addresses a defect or gap the repository already recorded, not one invented for this issue
One issue moved READY to ACTIVE to VERIFY to DONE through the command surface
The evidence attached to it is a command and its result, not a narrative
The next ready issue after it is derived, not chosen
issues.risk: Choosing a milestone to make the demonstration easy would defeat the purpose.
